attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own Substack post, in his own voice. It is not quoted from anyone else.

semantics.note: The 'such... that they can't' structure blames the inability to fact-check on superficial understanding, so causal is the right kind. 'Begin to' is kept and nothing is hedged. The proposition matches the sentence.

contract.note: An informed reader would take 'can't begin to' as no meaningful ability, not just unreliability, so the reading is fair and ordinary. The definition of self-checking, the limits on outside help and the 2025 window were all chosen by the evaluator, so interpretation decides the result. The causal mechanism has no measure the speaker supplied.

evidence.note: Preprint from 2025-03-24, inside the window. It is a controlled self-evaluation without retrieval. GPT-4o and GLM-4 correctly assessed about 38–43% of the false claims they had generated themselves. That is meaningful error identification, despite many abstentions and more wrong assessments on their own output.
Preprint from 2025-03-05, inside the window. The method adds trained internal-state probes, which is an extra component, so it does not show unaided self-checking. Context only.

reviews.rationale: The contract's contradiction condition is met. In e1 the models, with no retrieval, correctly flagged a substantial share of their own false claims, which goes against 'can't begin to.' The same study shows weaknesses: many abstentions and more wrong assessments on their own output. These limits do not restore a total inability. No study in the packet tests the superficial-understanding mechanism. But the claimed effect is contradicted, so the causal claim fails under the contract.
